title: A multimodal dataset of EEG, eye-tracking, and physiological signals during smartphone interaction
description: This multimodal dataset comprises simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG), eye-tracking, photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) recordings from 23 healthy adult participants during two experimental conditions: naturalistic smartphone interaction and standardized video viewing. Hardware-based TTL synchronization enables precise temporal alignment across all physiological modalities, facilitating investigation of neural and physiological responses to digital device interaction.
methods_description: Data were acquired using a 64-channel EEG cap and head-mounted eye tracker with concurrent PPG and GSR recordings. Two experimental conditions were implemented: a 10-minute smartphone interaction condition using participants' personal devices, and a 5-minute video viewing condition. Hardware-based TTL synchronization pulses (five pulses at ~1-second intervals marking session boundaries, with additional pulses every 20 seconds) were embedded in both EEG and eye-tracking data streams to enable cross-modal temporal alignment.
